oracle_policy: Source truth is frozen from upstream published fixture expectations, not from support_learning detector output. Unknown page-level counts remain null. Capability expectation and topology requirements are separate and may never change source truth.

cases.oracle_evidence: Camelot quickstart/fixture publishes one 7x7 ruled table. PDF M2.4 still cannot bind its source blocks without crossing the table boundary, so it must fail closed rather than emit partial structure.
Camelot lattice regression explicitly asserts two tables for twotables_2.pdf. M2.4 still does not expose a defensible lines_strict candidate for this page, so this remains a recall observation.

Camelot lattice regression uses row_span_1.pdf as a row-spanning table fixture, and the pinned published Camelot benchmark CSV establishes one 40x4 table. M2.4 must recover that shape and demonstrate at least one rectangular row span; exact span coordinates are intentionally not invented as gold.

Camelot lattice regression uses column_span_2.pdf as a column-spanning table fixture, and the pinned published Camelot benchmark CSV establishes one 11x7 table. M2.4 must recover that shape and demonstrate at least one rectangular column span; exact span coordinates are intentionally not invented as gold.
Image-only fixture is a hard negative for the native-text PDF table pipeline. OCR is intentionally deferred as an optional later extension.

PyMuPDF test_strict_lines uses lines_strict on this fixture, and test_markdown publishes the complete 5x3 extracted table content. Upstream does not assert the total number of tables on the page, so page-level count is intentionally unknown.
